intended_object: The value set D(Q) of a quadratic form Q over a field: the set of nonzero elements of K (equivalently, units in K*) that Q represents. Inferred from the docstring. Over a general commutative semiring it is the set of represented units.
explanation: The body is {a : Rˣ | ∃ v, Q v = a}. Over a field the units are exactly the nonzero elements, so this is the textbook D(Q) = {a ∈ K* : a is represented by Q}, which the literature (Lam, Scharlau) defines as a subset of K*. The definition works over any commutative semiring, so it is not too narrow, and the docstring states plainly what it means beyond fields: the represented units, not all represented values. No issues with degenerate cases: 0 is not a unit, so it is excluded, exactly as in D(Q). I did not search Mathlib for a dedicated value-set definition; the only related notion I am aware of is `Set.range Q`, which also contains non-units.
